messages:
maria: FYI support just escalated multiple latency complaints — p95 up ~2x, p99 ~3x starting ~02:45 UTC for a handful of customers (acme-prod, beta-retail). No deploy on record. Stack traces look like waiting on KV/prefix cache.

ashwin: got links to the alerts/dashboards? any correlation with GC or node restarts?

maria: dashboards here: https://grafana.redwood/short/prefix-cache. Topline: huge spike in prefix_cache_misses and evictions. No GC spikes. Noticed a node restart in us-west-2 at ~02:44 — likely warmup problem + thrash.

helena: can you paste the minutes-level metrics for the last 20m? curious about hit ratio and eviction rate.

maria: pasted metrics snippet:

```
prefix_cache_hits_total 120312
prefix_cache_misses_total 85290
prefix_cache_evictions_total 40234
prefix_cache_size_bytes 12884901888
prefix_cache_capacity_bytes 12884901888
prefix_cache_avg_key_len 48
```

miss ratio ~0.41 and evictions are high -> constant churn.

ton y: (reacts :thinking:) any recent changes to cache key instrumentation or normalization? those can explode key cardinality.

maria: good call. I grepped the request logs for cache_key usage and found inconsistent separators — some keys have a tab, others space. example logs:

```
INFO cache_put key="user:1234\tsession:abcd" route=chat
INFO cache_get miss key="user:1234 session:abcd" route=chat
```

looks like a recent helper lib change in request serialization could have switched from `\t` to ` ` for one code path. That would make the cache treat the same logical prefix as different keys -> cardinality blowup.

jenna: customer repro (from support):
```
# repro quickly hitting same route
for i in {1..200}; do 
  curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood/v1/chat -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -d '{"prefix":"hello","user":"1234"}' &
done
```
I see latency climb after ~50 concurrent requests.

sre-bot: ALERT: high-prefix-cache-eviction-rate detected on us-west-2 cluster-5 (threshold=20000/15m)

ashwin: action plan (short term):
- bump prefix cache capacity from 12GB -> 18GB on cluster-5 (quick config flip, risk: memory headroom)
- enable pinning for top-100 prefixes (hot set) to avoid eviction storms
- deploy small normalization shim (server-side) to canonicalize separators to `:` before writing cache keys (safe, idemp)

helena: +1 but need rollback plan. Also suggest enabling prefix warmup job to populate cache from recent hot keys on restart. Warmup reduces the post-restart miss spike.

tony: I can run warmup and do the capacity bump. Warmup script (dry-run showed ~80% of current hot set populated):
```
# warmup.sh (runs from ops bastion)
HOT_KEYS_FILE=/tmp/hot_prefixes.txt
while read k; do
  curl -s -X GET "http://cluster-5-cache.local/warmup?key=$(urlencode \"$k\")"
done < $HOT_KEYS_FILE
```
will run with 6 parallel workers.

maria: normalization shim — how intrusive? can it be a middleware so we don't need full rollout?

ashwin: yes middleware in front of cache layer only. code snippet (pseudo):
```
function canonicalize(key) {
  // replace whitespace and tabs with ':' and collapse multiples
  return key.replace(/\s+/g, ':').toLowerCase();
}
```
we'll A/B behind a feature flag for 15m then flip.

jenna: will inform affected customers that we're applying mitigation and expect p95 to improve in ~10-20m. :thumbsup:

helena: medium-term fix items (tracked in ticket):
- audit all call sites that build cache keys (js/service, go/runtime)
- add unit tests for canonicalization
- add telemetry: unique_prefix_count per-route and normalized_key_rate
- consider switching eviction policy to windowed-LFU if churn stays high

ashwin: who owns the audit? tony? helena?

tony: I can start audit of go/runtime and ops scripts. maria can cover SDK paths (js/python).

maria: will open incident ticket and link this thread. I'll run the middleware feature flag and coordinate warmup + capacity bump now. tagging @oncall.

sre-bot: oncall change: @alice is now on-call for cluster-5 (shift start)

ashwin: risk of warmup + capacity bump = higher memory use. we should monitor OOMs. set alert for cache_memory_usage > 85% and OOM kill rate.

maria: ack. I'll add alerts and annotate dashboards. timeline:
- t+2m: flip middleware feature flag (cache read canonicalize only)
- t+5m: increase cache capacity to 18GB
- t+8m: run warmup script (6 workers)
- t+15m: check p95/p99 and evictions.

jenna: recorded customer-facing note: "We're aware of elevated latency, rolling mitigations now. We'll update in 30m."

ashwin: post-mortem followups: verify that a PR didn't accidentally change separator. if so, revert and add pre-merge checks.

helena: also add a short-lived metric: cache_key_variants_per_logical_prefix — will help detect this class of bug automatically.

maria: thanks everyone — I’ll post updates here. current status: middleware flipped, capacity bump scheduled. next update in ~12m. :hourglass_flowing_sand:
